title: Kernelized Attention with Differentiable Spectral Filters: Beyond Dot-Product Compatibility for Long-Context Transformers
description: Proposes replacing the standard scaled dot-product attention with a learnable, kernelized compatibility function parameterized as a spectral filter bank. The compatibility between query and key is computed via a low-rank decomposition of a learned positive-definite kernel matrix, enabling sub-quadratic complexity while capturing richer relational structures than the dot product allows.
summary: The dot-product compatibility function (gap_45901fb5) limits the expressiveness of attention by assuming linear interactions between query and key, while the fixed 1/√d_k scaling (gap_29ccef3b) relies on unrealistic independence assumptions. This idea introduces a learnable kernel function K(q,k) = φ_θ(q)^T M_θ ψ_θ(k) where M_θ is a low-rank positive semi-definite matrix parameterized via a spectral decomposition learned end-to-end. The kernel is approximated using random Fourier features with learnable spectral distributions, yielding O(N d log d) complexity instead of O(N^2). An adaptive temperature parameter τ_θ per head replaces the fixed √d_k scaling, learned via a small hypernetwork that estimates the actual covariance structure of queries and keys. This directly addresses the resolution limitation from averaging (gap_65066c4d) by allowing the kernel to learn sharp, position-specific compatibility patterns. The method will be evaluated on long-document understanding (e.g., LED, Longformer benchmarks) and long-video temporal reasoning tasks, where quadratic attention is prohibitive.
method: Design a parameterized kernel K(q,k) = φ_θ(q)^T M_θ ψ_θ(k) where M_θ = U_θ Λ_θ U_θ^T is a learned low-rank PSD matrix with rank r << d, and φ_θ, ψ_θ are learned MLP projections with residual connections to preserve identity mapping.

Replace the fixed 1/√d_k scaling with a learned temperature τ_θ per head, parameterized by a lightweight hypernetwork that estimates the empirical covariance Σ_{qk} from a minibatch of query-key pairs via exponential moving average.

Approximate the kernel via orthogonal random Fourier features (ORF) where the spectral distribution is parameterized as a learnable mixture of Gaussians, enabling sub-quadratic attention with O(N d log d) complexity.

Integrate the module as a drop-in replacement for standard multi-head attention in a Transformer (e.g., T5 or Llama) and train on long-context language modeling (PG-19, BookCorpus) and long-video action recognition (Charades, Something-Something).

Evaluate efficiency (FLOPs, wall-clock time vs sequence length), quality (perplexity, BLEU, accuracy), and attention entropy to measure whether learnable kernels reduce resolution loss compared to standard dot-product.

evaluation.novelty: While kernelized attention exists (e.g., linear attention, Performer), no prior work combines learnable spectral filter banks with adaptive per-head temperature and differentiable kernel learning in a single unified framework for long-context transformers.
evaluation.feasibility: Implementation is feasible using existing JAX/PyTorch libraries with standard Transformer backbones; the main cost is hyperparameter tuning for the spectral rank r and the number of Fourier features, but training is within ~2× the compute of a baseline Performer.
evaluation.impact: If successful, this would provide a principled replacement for dot-product attention that scales linearly with sequence length, adapts to data statistics, and captures more complex query-key interactions—directly impacting long-context LLMs, video understanding, and genomic sequence modeling.
evaluation.rigour: The approach is grounded in kernel theory (Mercer's theorem, random Fourier features), has well-defined complexity bounds, and will be evaluated on established benchmarks with controlled ablations against Performer, Linformer, and standard full-attention baselines.
risks: The learned kernel may collapse to the standard dot product during training, providing no additional benefit while adding overhead.
Random Fourier feature approximation error may degrade quality on tasks requiring precise token-level attention (e.g., NER, parsing).
Training stability may suffer due to the additional learned parameters in the kernel and temperature modules, requiring careful initialization and learning rate tuning.
